query: For refractory high-entropy alloys intended for high-temperature and irradiation-exposed applications, what intervention could improve mechanical performance while maintaining thermal and irradiation stability? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention, its mechanism, the predicted improvement relative to an appropriate baseline, the conditions under which it should hold, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment that could falsify it.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a nanocrystalline structure through composition change in refractory high-entropy alloys will improve mechanical performance by 25% in terms of yield strength at high temperatures (above 800°C) and under irradiation conditions, compared to conventional coarse-grained alloys, due to the enhanced grain boundary strengthening mechanism.
generation.intervention: Introduction of nanocrystalline structure through composition optimization
generation.uncertainty: The actual improvement may vary depending on the specific composition and processing conditions, and the irradiation stability may be affected by other factors such as defect accumulation and microstructural evolution.

falsification_experiment.design: Tensile testing and microstructural characterization of nanocrystalline and conventional coarse-grained refractory high-entropy alloys after irradiation to 10 dpa at 800°C
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the yield strength of the nanocrystalline alloy is not at least 15% higher than that of the conventional alloy, the hypothesis is falsified.
